about: Editorial: the redlining story's twelve D areas as a set, for the story page and its menu sheet only. No store section, no print files for sale, no plate. Written by tools/stories/redlining/boxes.py; do not edit by hand.
title: Richmond's twelve D areas, 1937 and today
subtitle: The Home Owners' Loan Corporation's 1937 map of Richmond on the ground, and each area it graded D, "Hazardous," as it stands now
note: The 1937 map shows buildings standing today that the city dates to 1937 or before, and Jackson Ward's from the 1925 and 1952 Sanborn maps; most others standing then are gone and not drawn. Box notes paraphrase the 1937 area descriptions. Working draft, not for sale.
credit: Drawn by Chris Busse with isoscape  ·  Grades: Home Owners' Loan Corporation, 1937 (National Archives, RG 195, via FRASER); outlines redrawn with Claude from the public-domain scan, positioned with OpenStreetMap street corners (ODbL)  ·  Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)  ·  Elevation: USGS 3DEP  ·  Year built: City of Richmond
ground_note: The ground is today's, from lidar, except in Jackson Ward, where the Turnpike's trench is filled for 1937.

boxes.title: D1, Jackson Ward, Apostle Town and Navy Hill
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: 95% Black, incomes of $350–750, one home in five owner-occupied, houses forty years old and more. Since: Gilpin Court (1943) on Apostle Town; the Turnpike, now I-95 and I-64; VCU's medical campus on most of Navy Hill.

boxes.title: D2, Washington Park, around Cheatwood Avenue
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: flat ground, frame houses, a population the form recorded as entirely Black, half of homes owner-occupied. Its neighbor C7's form faults C7 for lying too near D2. Since: 72% of the houses the city dates here were built 1938–1977.

boxes.title: D3, Oak Park, along Laburnum Avenue
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937 the form found "mostly woods and bushes" and practically no homes. Since: the woods are built over, 700 buildings in today's OpenStreetMap, with shops along Laburnum Avenue.

boxes.title: D4, Around Hunt and Hazelhurst Avenues
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: described as the same as Oak Park, D3: frame houses, a population it recorded as entirely Black, half owner-occupied. Since: about half the houses the city dates here are from before 1937, most of the rest from 1938–1977.

boxes.title: D5, Fairmount and the blocks around Mosby Court
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: frame houses about fifteen years old, a population the form recorded as 75% Black, one home in three owner-occupied. Since: Mosby Court (1962), for families the 17th Street renewal displaced; I-64 runs 3.3 km through it.

boxes.title: D6, Union Hill and the slopes of Church Hill
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: flats and frame houses forty years old, a population the form recorded as 80% Black and increasing. Since: more of 1937 stands here than in any other D area; 68% of the houses the city dates were built by then.

boxes.title: D7, Fulton
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: frame houses fifty years old, "bad" repair, no mortgage money, a population the form recorded as 80% Black. Since: called a slum in 1967 and cleared by the late 1980s; Historic Fulton Memorial Park stands on the ground.

boxes.title: D8, Randolph and Oregon Hill
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: brick flats and frame houses, a population the form recorded as 95% Black, families moving in from D1. Since: the Randolph renewal (1973) and the Downtown Expressway, 3.3 km of it through D8, across Randolph and Oregon Hill.

boxes.title: D9, Beside Maymont, then mostly vacant
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937 the form found vacant land, "practically undeveloped and inaccessible," and graded it D before anyone lived there. Since: 95% of the houses the city dates here were built 1938–1977.

boxes.title: D10, South of the river, around Bainbridge and Perry Streets
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: frame houses about 25 years old in poor repair, a population the form recorded as 95% Black, two homes in five owner-occupied. Since: about half the houses the city dates here were standing by 1937.

boxes.title: D11, Manchester, around Cowardin Avenue
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: the one D area the form recorded as white, "Laboring Whites," with the highest incomes of any D area. Since: 36% of the buildings the city dates here are from 2000 or later, the most of any D area.

boxes.title: D11.5, Blackwell
boxes.subtitle: Graded D, "Hazardous," in 1937; seen today
boxes.note: In 1937: frame houses about 25 years old, a population the form recorded as 95% Black, three homes in ten owner-occupied, mortgage money at 35–40% of appraisal. Since: 464 scattered-site public housing units, built in 1970.
